The playbook (NL-005#NL-005-S02, NL-031#NL-031-S02) specifies an Enterprise onboarding range of **8–10 weeks**, while the observed Q2 average is **8.7 weeks** (NL-012#NL-012-S06, NL-031#NL-031-S03). Thus, the observed average sits within the documented range but is closer to the upper end.

The longer duration versus simpler plans (Starter: 3.5 weeks, Growth: 5.2 weeks) is driven by Enterprise‑specific requirements that simpler plans do not have (NL-012#NL-012-S06, NL-005#NL-005-S02, NL-031#NL-031-S02):

- **Security reviews and SSO configuration** – Enterprise accounts require custom SAML/OIDC single sign-on and security audits (NL-012#NL-012-S06, NL-005#NL-005-S02, NL-015#NL-015-S04).
- **Permission mapping** – Complex Active Directory/Okta permission mapping to replicate internal folder hierarchies; this is the largest delay source (45% of onboarding delays) (NL-012#NL-012-S06, NL-015#NL-015-S04).
- **Custom data‑retention and DPA validation** – Enterprise contracts involve custom DPAs, key rotation (BYOK), and compliance checks (NL-005#NL-005-S09, NL-015#NL-015-S04).
- **OCR processing of scanned PDFs** – Many enterprise customers have legacy scanned documents requiring OCR to meet the 85% citation correctness threshold (NL-012#NL-012-S06, NL-015#NL-015-S04, NL-005#NL-005-S02).
- **Extended UAT** – Up to 3 weeks of user acceptance testing for internal security and audit teams (NL-005#NL-005-S09).

Simpler plans (Starter, Growth) typically upload clean, public‑facing documents, have no complex RBAC, and use standard SSO, allowing a faster 2–6 week process (NL-012#NL-012-S06, NL-031#NL-031-S02). The extra administrative and technical steps in Enterprise accounts inherently extend the timeline to the observed 8.7‑week average.
